title: BECE English Studies: Grammar & Structure - English Studies - Parts of Speech - Adjectives
subject: English Studies

questions.q:
Choose the correct comparative form to complete the sentence:
"Of the two brothers, Paul is the _____."
questions.explain: When comparing two subjects, the comparative degree is used. The comparative form of 'tall' is 'taller'. The superlative 'tallest' is used when comparing three or more.
questions.subject: English Studies

questions.q: Which of the following sentences places the adjectives in the correct order?
options: She bought a beautiful large wooden dining table.
She bought a large beautiful wooden dining table.
She bought a wooden large beautiful dining table.
She bought a beautiful wooden large dining table.
questions.explain: The standard order of adjectives is Opinion (beautiful) -> Size (large) -> Age -> Shape -> Color -> Origin -> Material (wooden) -> Purpose (dining). Therefore, 'beautiful large wooden' is correct.
questions.subject: English Studies

questions.q:
Which option places the adjectives in the correct order to complete the sentence?
"She went to the market to buy _____ apples."
questions.explain: The correct order begins with the demonstrative determiner (those), followed by size (big), and then color (red).
questions.subject: English Studies

questions.q:
Identify the correct superlative form to fill the gap:
"Mount Everest is the _____ mountain in the world."
questions.explain: When comparing more than two things or declaring something to hold the top degree, the superlative form is used. For the short adjective 'high', we add '-est' to make 'highest'.
